command:
set -euo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

delly --version > dellyver.txt 2>&1
DV=$(awk '/Delly version/{print $3}' dellyver.txt)

echo "== delly 2.6.0: the subcommand is 'sr', NOT 'call' =="
delly sr -g ref.fa -o sv.bcf sample.bam > delly.log 2>&1 || { tail -20 delly.log; exit 1; }
grep 'Sample:' delly.log | tee delly-stats.txt

test -s sv.bcf || { echo "delly produced no BCF"; exit 1; }
MAD=$(sed -n 's/.*MAD=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' delly-stats.txt)
UDP=$(sed -n 's/.*UniqueDiscordantPairs=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' delly-stats.txt)
RS=$(sed -n 's/.*ReadSize=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' delly-stats.txt)
# delly's image ships no bcftools, so the CALL is asserted in the next task. What IS
# assertable here is that delly saw the evidence at all -- a library it cannot model
# (MAD=0) or with no discordant pairs would yield a green run and an empty call set.
test "$MAD" -gt 0 || { echo "delly measured MAD=0 -- no insert-size distribution to model"; exit 1; }
test "$UDP" -gt 0 || { echo "delly found no discordant pairs -- nothing to call from"; exit 1; }
{
printf 'delly_version\t%s\n' "$DV"
printf 'read_size\t%s\n' "$RS"
printf 'insert_mad\t%s   (assert >0 -- a fixed fragment length gives MAD=0, which delly cannot model)\n' "$MAD"
printf 'unique_discordant_pairs\t%s   (assert >0 -- the paired-end signal delly calls from)\n' "$UDP"
} | tee -a delly-stats.txt
echo "DELLY RAN"
